env_vars.description: List of environment variable settings for git-quick-stats control. Each item defines a variable name, value, and description based on documented options. Use 'value' only if a non-empty value is required; omit for flag-like behavior where only presence matters (but note: git-quick-stats uses environment variables with values for all documented settings). All variables are exported with `export VAR=VALUE` in the template. See 'name' for exact variable names used in documentation. 'value' must be a string or number; empty string allowed where unset is valid (e.g., no pathspec). For list-valued settings (e.g., _GIT_LOG_OPTIONS with multiple flags), join with space via `join(' ')` filter in template usage — here, store as list and template uses `default('') | default(quote)` which produces quoted space-joined value only when needed — but per spec, template MUST use only standard filters: hence, template uses `| default('')` and omits quotes, leaving quoting to consumer (shell interprets unquoted value as-is if no special chars). To preserve strict spec compliance, values MUST be pre-joined strings (space-separated) where multiple tokens needed, and 'value' field is always a string or number. Hence, we define items with 'value' as string or number, never list-of-strings. Therefore, items schema: 'name' -> string, 'value' -> string|number, 'description' -> string. We omit 'value' from items schema if it's optional/empty — but schema requires 'default' — so we include it with default empty string where unset is valid. For boolean-like behavior (e.g., _GIT_MERGE_VIEW exclusive), use string values 'enable', 'exclusive', 'disable' as documented. See manpage: '_GIT_MERGE_VIEW=enable' or 'exclusive'. Similarly, _GIT_LIMIT is numeric (e.g., 20). For _GIT_PATHSPEC, value is space-separated pathspec pattern (e.g., ':!build/*'). All documented env vars are included below. We define a flat item schema per spec: items -> {name: {type: string}, value: {type: string|number}, description: {type: string, default: ''}}. Note: spec forbids nested objects in 'default'; so we do NOT use {type: object}. Instead, define items as list-of-strings via items -> FLAT map. Per spec, items must be FLAT map field-name -> {type, default, description}. So we define: items: {name: {type: string, default: '', description: 'Environment variable name (e.g., _GIT_SINCE)'}, value: {type: string, default: '', description: 'Value assigned to the variable (empty string means unset or default)'}}, description: {type: string, default: '', description: 'Human-readable description of the setting'}. But wait: spec says 'items' as a FLAT map of field-name -> {...}, NOT array of objects. So we define items schema as: {name: {type: string, default: '', description: ''}, value: {type: string, default: '', description: ''}, description: {type: string, default: '', description: ''}} — this is a flat map of fields, not array of objects. Yes, per spec: 'for a list-of-objects, add `items` as a FLAT map field-name -> {type, default, description} (NOT {type:object, properties:{…}})'. So items = {name: ..., value: ..., description: ...}, each with type string, default empty string (or for value, string is fine since all documented values are strings/numbers). For value, we use type: string because all documented values are strings (e.g., '2017-01-20', '20', 'enable', etc.). Even numeric values like _GIT_LIMIT are passed as string in shell (export _GIT_LIMIT=20). So type: string for value is correct. Thus, items schema: name: {type: string, default: '', description: 'Environment variable name'}, value: {type: string, default: '', description: 'Value (stringified)'} — but spec says 'default' must be a BARE scalar — so we use default: '' for string. Yes, empty string is a bare scalar. We include only documented env vars. We list them from manpage: _GIT_SINCE, _GIT_UNTIL, _GIT_LIMIT, _GIT_LOG_OPTIONS, _GIT_PATHSPEC, _GIT_MERGE_VIEW, _MENU_THEME, _GIT_BRANCH. That's 8 documented env vars. We create 8 items. Each item has name, value (string or numeric, stored as string), description. For _GIT_PATHSPEC, default is '' (unset), value example is ':!build/*'. For _GIT_LIMIT, value is '20'. For _GIT_BRANCH, default is '' (use current branch), example is 'master'. We include 'description' field as per spec — but items schema only needs name/value/description as flat map fields.
